about: The mildest of the three Original blends from Adrian Magnus, made with non-aged tobacco at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. It launched at InterTabac 2025 alongside Original Medium and Original Strong.
notes: Maker's spec table says Ecuador Habano wrapper, but its own description calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Shade and adds Honduras to the filler. Trade press calls the line Originals. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

about: The middle blend of the three Original cigars from Adrian Magnus, made with non-aged tobacco at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. It launched at InterTabac 2025.
notes: Maker's description says the blend is entirely Nicaraguan, but its spec table and Cigar Coop list Nicaraguan and Dominican filler. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

about: The strongest of the three Original blends from Adrian Magnus, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over non-aged tobacco. It is made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic and launched at InterTabac 2025.
notes: Maker's strength scale shows medium-strong; Cigar Coop described it as full strength. Maker's description mentions only Nicaraguan filler, while its spec table adds Dominican. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

about: One of three XSO blends from Adrian Magnus, made with non-aged tobacco at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. The line launched at InterTabac 2025.
notes: The maker's site lists a San Andres Mexico wrapper, but the launch coverage (Cigar Coop) gave a shade-grown Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and no Pennsylvania filler. Cigar Coop called it medium to full. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

about: The medium blend of the three XSO cigars from Adrian Magnus, wrapped in a broadleaf leaf over non-aged tobacco. It is made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic and launched at InterTabac 2025.
notes: The origin of the broadleaf wrapper is not disclosed. Maker's description says 100% Nicaraguan tobacco from Jalapa, but its spec table and Cigar Coop list Nicaraguan and Dominican filler. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

about: The strongest of the three XSO blends from Adrian Magnus, made with non-aged tobacco at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. The line launched at InterTabac 2025.
notes: Maker's spec table and Cigar Coop say San Andres Mexico wrapper, but the maker's own description says dark Broadleaf. Maker's strength scale shows medium-strong; Cigar Coop called it full. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

about: The mildest of the three blends in Montego, a value-priced line from Adrian Magnus. It is made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic and launched at InterTabac 2025.
notes: The maker labels the line Montego MNTG. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

about: The middle blend of the three in Montego, a value-priced line from Adrian Magnus. It is made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic and launched at InterTabac 2025.
notes: Maker's spec table and Cigar Coop say Ecuadorian Habano wrapper; the maker's description calls it Ecuadorian Shade. Maker's strength scale shows medium while its text and Cigar Coop say medium to full. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

about: The top blend of the three in Montego, a value-priced line from Adrian Magnus, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan filler. It is made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic and launched at InterTabac 2025.
notes: The maker's Robusto page lists a Nicaraguan binder, while its Toro and Belicoso pages and Cigar Coop say Indonesian. The maker rates it 3 out of 5 (medium); Cigar Coop described it as the boldest Montego. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

about: The youngest of the aged lines from Adrian Magnus, made with long-filler tobacco the maker says is aged five years. It is rolled in the Dominican Republic and was shown to US retailers at the 2025 PCA trade show.
notes: Wrapper is agreed as Ecuadorian Connecticut. The maker lists an Ecuadorian binder with Honduran, Dominican and Nicaraguan filler; Stogie Press and a retailer list Dominican binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. Strength is disputed: the maker's scale shows light, Stogie Press says medium, and one retailer sells it as full.
